svg.title: Maknae container architecture
svg.desc: UML deployment view of the Maknae container architecture.
svg.text: design/container-architecture.md, drawn. Eight containers, three planes. Solid is ratified; dashed is proposed.
Visual grammar borrowed from the Microkosmos SV-1 deployment views. Their RMF apparatus — authorization boundary, CNSSI 1253
categorization, control-inheritance taxonomy — is deliberately absent: those answer an Assess-Only package, and Maknae has none yet.
The only trusted code. Nothing transits without it.
registry and audit writer live here.
The only path out. Compromise here
Untrusted by design. Stateless: holds no durable state (§1.5).
The agent. Does the work, under
Was lake rw / dreamer rw / kernel ro — the untrusted
containers held write on label state while the only trusted
one was read-only. Corrected by KLC 6.1; writes are brokered
Append-only; export is a later kernel-mediated feature
Tier 0. Changes arrive as signed commits, never writes
Per-service tmpfs. Never a named persistent volume
BASE DEPLOYMENT — RBAC. Authorization is decided by maknae-authz-basic behind the maknae-security seam. The seam exposes a versioned interface, and
a backend behind it is a LINKED CRATE inside maknaed exactly as maknae-authz-basic is today — not a container. No box on this diagram changes when a
backend is added or swapped; that is what the seam is for (ADR-0004).
One image ships today: the kernel, FROM scratch on a static musl target, built with cargo auditable. Six of the eight containers are Proposed, and
there is no Compose file or Kubernetes manifest in the tree.
